rationale: The ordered-monomial description is false before normality is assumed: arbitrary generated star-algebras require arbitrary words in T and T*. The repair defines the general word algebra and derives the ordered form only in the normal case.

The definition says spectral nonnegativity does not imply positivity without self-adjointness. The companion is explicitly a counterexample: its Statement refuted is the opposite universal implication and its witness J has spectrum {0} but a non-real quadratic value. There is no A/B inconsistency.
The explanatory sentence falsely called an arbitrary bounded normal operator unitary. Replacing that adjective by normal preserves the intended generated-star-algebra distinction.

The item omits thm-rationals-countable from its local citations, but the fixed enumeration of Q is an elementary standard consequence already established elsewhere in the library and a competent reader closes this single bookkeeping step immediately. The quotient-space construction, almost-disjoint family, and contradiction are unaffected; no statement, witness, computation, or choice scope is false. Fatal-only Step 7 therefore makes no content edit.

The conclusion relative to every Hilbert basis is load-bearing and was not exported by the cited diagonal example or definition. The repair declares and cites thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent, whose claims 2-3 give exactly the needed basis-independence under Countable Choice; the manifest, proof contract, and cross-batch edge input were synchronized.
The sequence is explicitly indexed by N with 0 included, but the displayed series began at 1 and omitted B_0. The repair changes the lower index to 0.
Allowing an empty normal form makes max_j |a_j| undefined on X empty. The repair requires m at least 1 and gives the canonical one-term zero presentation for the empty space.
The strong-convergence clause did not explicitly require a uniformly bounded sequence. The repair states pointwise E-a.e. convergence together with sup_n ||f_n||_infinity finite.

Step 2.1 cites the wrong one of the two immediately preceding parity facts: the complement of E is cofinite exactly when E is finite, and step 1.1 already proves E infinite. The nonemptiness aside is also reversed, but neither error affects the explicit even-set witness or the conclusion and a competent reader repairs the inference instantly from step 1.1 and F1. Under the fatal-only rule no content edit is warranted.
The statement's series began at 1 although the sequence and the proof's partial sums are zero-based. Both weak and strong series are repaired to begin at 0.

The consumer's zero-based proof is correct. The inconsistency was wholly in def-projection-valued-measure's formerly 1-based display, which has its own confirmed-fatal rejection and repair. No change to this item is warranted.
The spectral PVM is natively defined only on sigma(T), while E({lambda}) was used for every complex lambda. The repair explicitly extends E by E(A)=E(A intersect sigma(T)) for Borel A in C.

Undefined traces alone do not refute an extension. The repaired statement is the precise obstruction actually proved: no linear functional whose domain contains the trace class and the two shift products can both agree with the ordinary trace and be cyclic on S*,S, because linearity would force tau(P_0)=0 while agreement gives tau(P_0)=1. The title, item proof, manifest mirror, and proof contract were synchronized.
The formula applied E to intervals and endpoint singletons in R although E was natively defined only on sigma(T). The repair declares the zero extension E(A)=E(A intersect sigma(T)).
A2 falsely quantified over every nonzero measurable function. The needed quotient-space fact applies to representatives of a nonzero L2 class; the repair states exactly that condition.

The cited counterexample establishes one multiplication operator with no eigenvectors, not a general almost-everywhere assertion at non-atomic points. The repair states exactly the example's supplied conclusion.

The proof transferred convergence between horizon-scaled dyadic partition sequences that have different grid points. The repair states fixed-horizon convergence and simultaneous convergence only for prescribed countable horizon families, exactly as the supplier proves.

The Brownian process is indexed only on nonnegative time, while the statement quantified over intervals with negative endpoints. The repair restricts all interval and rational-endpoint quantifiers to [0,infinity).

The statement included nonpositive Holder exponents that the supplier does not state and that make the diagonal expression problematic for negative exponents. The repair restricts the claim to 0<alpha<1/2.

An arbitrary representative of an L2 Lebesgue class need not be Borel and therefore need not define the asserted predictable process. The repair explicitly chooses Borel representatives before forming deterministic integrands.

The complement calculation replaced M_t<a by M_t<=a before excluding an atom. The repair first derives atomlessness at a from the continuous maximum distribution function and then takes the valid complement.

The proof conditioned Z_t before proving integrability and used a bounded-factor rule on the unbounded factor Z_s. The repair first computes all required L1 norms by the Gaussian exponential moment, then cites the unbounded taking-out theorem under its product-integrability hypotheses.

The process was defined only through T although the cited martingale interface is indexed on all nonnegative times. The repair extends it constantly by g(B_T) after T and verifies all three time-order cases.

Nonnegativity of the maximum does not exclude an atom at zero. The repair bounds the zero event by the positive-level events and sends the level down to zero using continuity of the normal distribution function.
The zero-based sequence t=n evaluated the positive-time formula at n=0 and divided by zero. The repair uses t=n+1.

The proof asserted an unsupported T=0 extension outside the statement and suppliers, including the nontrivial claim that the augmented time-zero sigma-algebra is trivial. The repair removes that extraneous boundary assertion.
The semigroup proof used a common lower bound for the limit operator that the hypothesis stated only for the approximants. The repair includes A itself in the common-lower-bound hypothesis.

The cited scalar-normal and Brownian definitions do not export existence or the Fourier transform of the multivariate Gaussian used in the proof. The repair declares and cites the exact multivariate-normal definition and characteristic-function lemma.
The example allowed I empty while invoking a spectral theorem whose Hilbert-space hypothesis is nonzero and while taking an unqualified supremum. The repair explicitly assumes I nonempty.

The definition invoked the supplied semisimple-endomorphism notion for an unrestricted complex Lie algebra, although that notion is defined only in finite dimension. The repair states the required finite-dimensional hypothesis and synchronizes owned manifest and proof-contract mirrors.

A function defined only on the essential range cannot literally be composed with exceptional values of m outside that range. The repair uses a bounded Borel extension and notes independence modulo the null exceptional set.
A3 falsely described the range of M_g for arbitrary g; it is true for the indicator actually used. The repair narrows A3 to multiplication by an indicator and its exact range/kernel.

A3 attributed a general multiplier characterization to a definition that does not state it. The repair gives the elementary idempotence, symmetry and range calculation for the indicator actually used.

F3 falsely said the cited consistency theorems supply models containing the original ZFA continuum L. Their stated interface supplies a normal-space witness with a nonseparable closed pair. The repair derives bounded Tietze failure directly from that exact transferred witness.

Fact L4 attributed polynomiality of the semisimple adjoint part to a theorem whose public statement identifies the additive parts but does not state their polynomiality. The repair declares and cites the exact additive Jordan–Chevalley theorem that supplies the polynomial claim.

L1 cited only the derivation definition, whose interface explicitly defers proof that adjoint maps are derivations. The repair declares and cites the proposition that proves every adjoint map satisfies the derivation law.

The total-variation definition takes a supremum over countable partitions, but the proof bounded only finite partitions. The repair applies Cauchy--Schwarz to finite partial sums of each countable partition and passes to the monotone limit.

The approximation numbers and selected approximants were specified only for positive indices but then used as library sequences, whose domain is ℕ including 0. The repair supplies harmless index-zero values a_0(T)=||T|| and F_0=0 and states the singular-value identity on n≥1.

The scalar integral dependency defines the integral using nonzero level sets, not an arbitrary disjoint normal form. The repair explicitly regroups an arbitrary form by its finitely many values and uses finite additivity before invoking that definition.

L2 attributed global Killing-form nondegeneracy to root-decomposition and orthogonality interfaces that do not state it. The repair declares and cites Cartan's semisimplicity criterion for exactly that implication.

A3 attributed a concentration implication to the scalar-measure lemma, whose interface does not state it. The repair derives it directly from PVM multiplicativity before using the scalar-measure identity.
The convergence clause formed Phi_E(f) without assuming that the pointwise almost-everywhere limit f belongs to the bounded measurable domain of Phi_E. The repair states that hypothesis explicitly.

The convergence clause used f(T) without assuming that the almost-everywhere pointwise limit f is a bounded Borel function in the calculus domain. The repair adds the missing hypothesis and removes a duplicated adjective.
Step 1.1 used invariance with [H,f] instead of [f,H], producing the false sign [e,f]=-B(e,f)H_alpha. The repair uses B([e,f],H)=B(e,[f,H]) and obtains the correct positive sign.

The item used j≤n on an infinite-rank SVD system indexed by ℕ including 0 while identifying the remainder with the positive-index numerical singular value s_{n+1}(T). The repair relabels the system by positive integers and defines the zero-based n-term truncation with T_0=0.

A4 falsely asserted that Phi_E(z) is self-adjoint exactly when z is real on the ambient compact set, ignoring E-null nonreal points. The repair removes the unused equivalence and retains the valid normality calculation.

L1 reversed the consistency consequence for an extension and even concluded that the assumed-consistent base theory was inconsistent. The repair states the correct monotonicity of derivability and inconsistency of the extension augmented by the negated theorem.

The uniqueness proof used that an arbitrary PVM integral is a unital star-homomorphism, but none of its cited facts supplied that result. The repair declares and cites the exact PVM star-homomorphism theorem and refreshes the frontier ledger.

The proof applied the extension U directly to hf although h is merely Borel and hf need not be continuous. The repair proves U[q]=q(T)x for bounded Borel q by L2 approximation, then applies it to hf before using density.
With the stated inner-product convention, the representing functional is conjugate-linear in the domain variable. The definition now states the correct scalar behavior.
The cited compact-support definition did not define the asserted C2 class. The repair defines C2 locally and removes the inapposite citation.
The definition required pointwise equality X0=x although random variables are only specified almost surely in this setting. It now requires X0=x almost surely.
The formula was presented as though its input lay in D(A), but the bounded Cayley transform acts on all of H through the inverse resolvent. Both constituent maps are now typed with domain H.

Coordinatewise Brownian conditions did not ensure the vector process had independent coordinates or the required vector future-increment independence. The definition now states the vector Brownian filtration condition explicitly.
The stopping observation used sigma wedge tau_n as a localizing sequence, which need not tend to infinity. The original localizing sequence tau_n correctly localizes the stopped process.

The deterministic-time identification omitted the infinite deterministic time, for which the stopped sigma-algebra is the ambient sigma-algebra rather than any finite-time filtration. The two cases are now separated.
The Hilbert-space dimension convention relied on arbitrary orthonormal bases, whose existence needs full choice rather than the declared countable choice. The hypothesis and dependency now match.

The spectral projection notation used the unbounded Borel functional calculus while citing only a bounded predecessor interface. The exact local functional-calculus supplier is now declared and cited.
The predictability proof omitted the time-zero fiber from preimages of Borel sets. It now includes that measurable fiber explicitly.
The source-convention comparison had the self-adjoint generator sign reversed. The repaired relation is A=iG=-T for the stated exponential convention.
The definition asserted independence of approximation before that result was available. It now proves the assertion directly from the elementary isometry and density.
The adaptedness proof treated every coefficient as F_t-measurable even before its interval began. The repaired proof separates the zero summands from coefficients whose left endpoint is at most t.

The completion family quantified subsets without requiring an ambient measurable null superset, so some members need not belong to the ambient sigma-algebra. That measurability requirement is now explicit.

The predictable rectangles themselves are not an algebra, since complements require finite unions. The definition now correctly calls them a pi-system together with the whole space and takes their generated sigma-algebra.
The defining sum included an out-of-range partition increment. The index now runs from 1 through the number of partition intervals.
The truncated-sum index k(t) was not constrained to the valid partition endpoints and could be undefined at the boundary. Its maximum is now explicitly taken over 0 through m.
The sequential compactness characterization invoked arbitrary sequence selection while declaring only countable choice. The item now states and declares full choice.
The title narrowed the definition to closed operators although the statement intentionally defines the resolvent for a general unbounded operator. The title now matches the actual definition.

The item claimed to integrate an arbitrary Borel function on an abstract measurable space, where Borel is not defined. It now requires a Sigma-measurable function and uses that terminology throughout.

The definition applied the library's finite-dimensional dim interface to arbitrary ranges of a potentially infinite-rank compact operator. The repair first restricts the dimension equality to the finite-dimensional case and handles infinite rank only through infinitude and countability of the singular multiset.

L2 and the construction used the false negative-sign bracket formula, so the selected f actually produced -h_alpha. The repair derives the positive-sign identity from invariance and selects f with B(e,f)=2/alpha(H_alpha).
A5 falsely said every subset with zero orthogonal complement is dense. The repair states the correct equivalence for the closed linear span, which is exactly the object used in the maximality proof.

A3 claimed mere T-invariance made the ambient and restricted cyclic subspaces agree, overlooking the T* generators. The repair uses the actual reducing hypothesis, so both T and T* preserve the summand and the generated subspaces coincide.

Step 3.2 invoked dnu/dmu although its dependencies only described integration once a derivative was given. The repair adds the published Radon--Nikodym existence theorem and proves positivity, strict positivity under equivalence, and the resulting unitary explicitly.

A4 misstated the cited circle Cauchy formula by omitting the centre and radius-domain hypotheses. The repair restores |z-a|<r and 0<r<R, which exactly licenses the contour calculation centred at the isolated eigenvalue.

The definition misread the coding lemma as a homeomorphism between all Baire and Cantor space and attributed measure transport to it. The repair fixes Cantor space as the measured carrier, retains Baire space only for auxiliary real quantifiers, and cites the dedicated coin-measure interface.

A2 attributed the defining adjoint pairing to a theorem whose interface only lists algebraic identities. The repair cites the adjoint definition and the inner-product convention that actually supply the calculation, then refreshes the frontier ledger.

A4 attributed norm definiteness and the spectral disc bound to a vocabulary-only spectrum definition. Neither claim was needed: the calculus isometry in A1 directly proves the norm formula, so the repair removes the inaccurate fact and citation.

The support-ideal definition omitted singleton supports and G-invariance, so its stabilizer family was not shown to satisfy the normal-filter interface required by the Fraenkel–Mostowski theorem. The repair adds both clauses and verifies finite intersections and conjugation explicitly.

A7 cited a continuous-image theorem restricted to metric spaces although the character space is only known compact Hausdorff. The repair replaces it with the general compact-space theorem and refreshes the frontier ledger.

L3 falsely said the one-dimensional-root-space theorem states that 2gamma is not a root. The repair removes that inflated attribution and proves the no-double-root fact locally by a trace-of-commutator argument on the negative-multiple root spaces.

The conclusion promoted one-way consequences to equivalences without proving that U* partial implies U partial. The repair applies the established forward implication to U* and uses U**=U, then states precisely which projection identity is consequential.

The definition falsely claimed compatibility of the metric and order topologies in the ordered rational Urysohn space; the Fraïssé age imposes no such relation. The repair treats the order only as a distinguished rigidifying relation and removes the unused order-topology dependency.

The statement used a coordinate function on an arbitrary compact Hausdorff space, where no such function is defined. The repair quantifies over nonempty compact subsets K of C and explicitly identifies z as the coordinate restriction.

The definition called every local homeomorphism a chart of the manifold and then quantified over all such charts, making even the identity map fail differentiability under nonsmooth coordinates. The repair makes a manifold chart a member of the specified atlas and restricts map representatives accordingly.

The isomorphism alone did not identify chi(f(T)) with f(chi(T)); this needs the theorem that characters of C(K) are evaluations. The repair adds that dependency, states the composition argument explicitly, and refreshes the frontier ledger.

The definition claimed that downward coherence makes the levels of any subtree into a successor-menu sequence, but a subtree with nonempty levels may have leaves. The repair distinguishes predecessor coherence from the forward-successor condition and assigns the required pruning to the equivalence proof.

The proof included the zero-dimensional subspace but called its empty unit-sphere numerical range a singleton. The repair handles dimension zero as the empty convex set and dimension one as the singleton case.

The definition asserted maximal torality and the full root-space decomposition by invoking two theorems whose statements assume Choice, but the definition did not. The repair removes those redundant AC-dependent consequences while retaining the root-space/root definitions and the exact zero convention.

The approximating sequence used the undefined error 1/n at the library index n=0. The repair uses 1/(n+1) consistently in the construction, Cauchy estimate, choice-independence estimate, and uniqueness argument.

The CH remark falsely identified the natural stationary set of countable limit ordinals as a nonreflecting HYP witness. At beta=omega^2 its trace contains the displayed club. The repair distinguishes the separate CH construction, whose ladder separation is proved directly, from HYP.

L5 attributed opposite-root existence and nondegeneracy of the opposite-root pairing to suppliers that do not state those claims. The repair cites the exact owned corollary that states both conclusions.

Step 4.1 did not prove that all continuous multipliers form C*(I,M_t): it omitted uniform polynomial approximation and the isometric multiplier norm. The repair proves the norm formula, closedness, and both range inclusions, adding Stone--Weierstrass and refreshing the frontier ledger.

The rational-time proof only yields a stopping time after null sets are completed, but the filtration was not required to be complete. The example now uses the usual augmented natural filtration explicitly.
The assertion quantified compact intervals outside Brownian motion's nonnegative time domain. The interval is now required to lie in [0,infinity).
The completed-square center had the s and t weights attached to the wrong endpoints. The corrected center is (tx+sz)/(s+t).
The independence inference needed uniqueness of a multivariate normal law from its characteristic function, which was not supplied. The exact characteristic-function lemma is now declared and cited.
The standard-normal definition did not supply the asserted improper power integral. The repair proves divergence directly by lower bounds on dyadic intervals and monotone convergence.

The proof claimed the lower-exit probability followed by exchanging roles in a one-direction theorem. The complementary-event calculation already proves it, so the invalid extra inference was removed.
The cited quadratic-variation definition did not define the example's varying-horizon dyadic family. The finite terminal sum is now defined directly and no unsupported interface is cited.
The cutoff construction cited a topological compact-set lemma that did not supply smoothness. It now cites the exact smooth-step cutoff lemma and only claims the boundedness actually used.

The stopping-time proof used completion without assuming the usual augmentation and also misstated the dyadic ceiling bound. The filtration and bound are now exact, and finiteness uses the cited exit law.
The statement claimed stopping at any bounded domain although the proof treated only origin-centred discs. The claim is now restricted to exactly the proved disc exits.
The example identified the elementary and general integrals without citing the compatibility clause. The general-integral definition is now declared and cited for that bridge.

The left-step integrands have unbounded Brownian coefficients and are not elementary under the page's bounded-coefficient definition. The repair treats them as predictable L2 integrands and proves the finite-sum identity by bounded truncations and the isometry.
The boundary discussion falsely said finite energy fails below n=2, despite its own valid n=1 case. The false sentence was removed.
The item attributed an ambient Brownian-interface choice hypothesis to the bare axiom definition. It now records only the explicit choice assumption actually supplied by that citation.

The localization allowed intervals not containing the initial state and wrote an unstopped differential after stopping. The index range now contains x and the stopped formula has the required indicators.
The complement calculation substituted a closed-event CDF for a strict event without stating atomlessness. The cited maximum-law density now explicitly supplies that equality.
The functional-analytic interfaces used in the proof assume full choice, while the item declared only weaker fragments. It now assumes and declares AC.
Under the shifted law P_x, the coordinates start at x_i and are not themselves standard Brownian motions. The statement and proof now correctly use W^(i)-x_i and the shifted target y_i-x_i.
The general multiplication-operator fact omitted the preimage under the multiplier in its spectral projection. It now states E(B)f=1_{m^{-1}(B)}f, specializing correctly to the position operator.

The nested post-hit Brownian processes are not an independent sequence, although their stopped excursion segments are iid. The false equivalence and conclusion were removed while retaining the valid excursion independence.
A1 attributed the defining adjoint pairing to an algebraic-properties theorem that does not state it. The repair adds and cites the Hilbert-space adjoint definition and refreshes the frontier ledger.

Step 1.2 claimed a constant finite sum solved the exponential ODE because the necessary t-powers were omitted. The repair defines the polynomial curve with t^k, verifies its ODE and initial value, and evaluates at t=1.

The theorem claimed polynomial construction of the square root without constructing polynomial approximants. The repair adds Stone--Weierstrass and the isometric norm-limit calculation, then refreshes the frontier ledger.

The witness e lies in sl_2, but the original dependencies only defined sl_2 and did not establish that it is semisimple. The repair cites the published nondegenerate Killing-form computation and Cartan's exact semisimplicity criterion.
The approximate eigenvector sequence used the undefined tolerance 1/n at the library index n=0. The repair replaces it by 1/(n+1), preserving the convergence argument for every index.

A2 attributed the defining pairing and conjugate-transpose matrix rule to an algebraic adjoint theorem that states neither. The repair cites the adjoint definition and computes J* directly on the orthonormal basis, then refreshes the frontier ledger.
Step 1.1 used the false sign z=-B(e,f)H_alpha. The repair derives z=B(e,f)H_alpha directly from Killing-form invariance and nondegeneracy and propagates the positive sign to alpha(z).

The fourth forcing coordinate ranges over lambda, so the canonical x-coordinate is a subset of lambda rather than a real. The repair gives its exact generic definition and transports the bounded Euclidean metric from the separate real parameter to each component, as in the primary source.

Step 2.2 reversed the use of spectral inclusion and could not show the Gelfand transform was nonvanishing. The repair uses the standard generated-algebra proof: adjoining x^{-1}, showing x-hat separates characters, and applying Stone--Weierstrass to recover x^{-1} in the smaller algebra.

The first witness used -alpha as a root without a supplier. The repair adds the exact opposite-root corollary and removes an inflated attribution of reducedness to the one-dimensional-root-space theorem.

The remark's claim that a cover has no point-finite refinement at all was false under the cited bare-containment refinement interface, because the empty family is always such a refinement. The repair states the intended failure: no point-finite open refining cover.

The facts falsely attributed nonexistence of 2alpha to the one-dimensional-root-space theorem. The repair attributes that consequence solely to the exact scalar-multiples corollary and removes the unused dependency.

A5 attributed sequential closedness and uniqueness of metric limits to the bare definition of metric topology. The repair cites the exact closure characterization and metric-limit uniqueness lemma and refreshes the dependency ledger.

The finite-common-refinement normalization began with G_1 and omitted the zeroth cover, so the asserted refinement and star containment failed at index zero. The repair intersects G_0 through G_n at stage n and updates the no-choice explanation accordingly.

L2 falsely attributed the claim that eigenspaces are exactly an endomorphism's invariant subspaces to an eigenvalue-existence corollary; the claim is false. The repair retains only the corollary's exact eigenvalue conclusion.

The proof needed openness of metric balls to form its product-open neighbourhood, but cited only the definitions of balls and the metric topology. The repair cites the exact open-ball theorem and refreshes the dependency ledger.

The final sentence falsely identified the adjoint zero-weight space g_0=h with the center, although the proof establishes only the common root kernel inside h. The repair states that exact common-kernel equality.

For finite nonzero lambda the fair-coin product is not the product of unnormalized counting measures, whose one-coordinate atoms have mass one. The repair identifies the finite factors as normalized counting measures on {0,1}.

The linearity identity attempted to add operators with incompatible source and target spaces. The repair introduces two same-typed operators for linearity and type-corrects the uniqueness, composition, and double-adjoint pairings throughout.
The complex-inner-product convention is conjugate-linear, not linear, in the second argument. The repair invokes only additivity there, which is the exact property the expansion needs.
The decreasing G-delta witness used V_1 through V_n, omitting V_0 and giving the empty intersection at n=0. The repair replaces it by the intersection of all V_k with k<=n.

A4 attributed sequential closedness to the definition of the metric topology, and neither that claim nor orthogonal-complement closedness was used. The repair removes the unused fact and dependencies and refreshes the ledger.
For the alpha-string through beta=alpha, the item confused beta+k alpha with k alpha and assigned p=q=1. The repair uses (k+1)alpha, obtaining k=-2,-1,0 and p=2,q=0,p-q=2.

The proof invoked the Banach-space fundamental theorem of calculus under a choice hypothesis too weak for its cited supplier. The repair declares countable and dependent choice, exactly matching that interface.
The proof applied its range-orthogonality identity with the wrong spectral parameter. The repair uses z=-i, which gives ker(T*+i) from ran(T-i).

The domain-density proof cited a monotone convergence theorem for real sequences instead of the measure-theoretic integral theorem and failed to state measurability on the abstract space. The repair declares the exact integral supplier and measurable functions.
A fact incorrectly asserted that a symmetric operator has purely imaginary quadratic forms. The repair states the correct skew-symmetric generator identity.

The claimed density proof inferred a vector-valued conclusion from positivity of a scalar weighted integral. The repair uses the Laplace approximate identity lambda Q_lambda y to converge directly to y and declares the choice scope required by its supplier.

The proof misapplied a support theorem for bounded normal operators to the unbounded operator T. The repair derives the support property internally by applying the already proved essential-range criterion to the identity function.

A fact treated the double adjoint as automatically defined, although its definition requires the adjoint domain to be dense. The repair explicitly restricts that assertion to the dense-adjoint-domain case used in the proof.

The Cayley-transform transport applied a PVM defined only on sigma(C) to subsets of the full circle. The repair explicitly extends the spectral PVM by zero off sigma(C) and makes the inverse transport at the omitted point 1 well typed.
The surjectivity argument invoked countable choice through its cited closed-range supplier while the theorem declared no choice. The repair adds and declares the exact countable-choice hypothesis.

A fact falsely asserted strong convergence for every uniformly bounded pointwise-convergent Borel approximation. The repair removes that overbroad claim and retains only the bounded-calculus properties actually used.

The proof asserted approximating sequences from closure without constructing them in the choice-sensitive setting and then used an unstated sequential-closedness principle. The repair proves closure is a subspace directly with ball approximations, requiring only finite choices and norm inequalities.
Step 2.1 falsely claimed k!=j makes both bracket terms vanish, overlooking l=i. The repair gives the exhaustive four-case analysis, including [E_ij,E_ki]=-E_kj and the zero-root Cartan case.

Density alone did not supply two countable approximating sequences in ZF, while the conclusion denied any such choice use. The repair explicitly forms the nonempty approximation sets, applies Countable Choice, and records that use.

The converse uniform-bounding proof used the reversed inequality g(n)<=n for a strictly increasing g. For k in [g(n),g(n+1)) the correct final comparison is g(n)<=k, which yields the required rapidity bound.
The stated subtraction of the four parallelogram identities did not produce the displayed Jensen identity. The repair specifies the correct subtraction: fourth identity from third.

The escape-line proof did not prevent the line from being contained in one of the later hyperplanes. The repair uses induction to choose u outside the first k-1 subspaces and v outside the kth, making every subspace exclude at most one parameter.

The proof took infima and suprema of complex finite sums, which are unordered, and its real diameter estimate used the wrong specialization. The repair proves the ordered argument over R with the correct tail diameter and handles C through real and imaginary parts.

The extension definition replaced complete-suborder maximal-antichain preservation by density of P1 in P2, and its remaining clauses then forced every extension to be equality. The repair restores Shelah's complete-suborder, class-containment, and old-condition clauses from Definition 7.9.

Conditions below a fixed p whose recorded tree contains a given node are dense only in the cone below p, not in all of UM, because conditions incompatible with p have no extension in that cone. The repair states the exact relative density used by genericity.

The interface unnecessarily restricted orthonormal families to Hilbert spaces despite claiming completeness was unused, and called the closed linear span merely a closed subspace. The repair defines orthonormality for inner-product spaces and reserves Hilbert basis for the complete case.

The proof replaced the required equality between rank and Cartan dimension by the weaker condition that a minimizing element lies in a Cartan subalgebra; every element lies in some Cartan only in special settings, and mere membership gives only h subset g^x. The repair chooses an existing regular semisimple element and invokes its Cartan centralizer.

The proof and statement are correct for arbitrary inner-product spaces. The sole mismatch was the cited orthonormal-family interface, now repaired under its own targeted rejection to cover inner-product spaces; this consumer needs no content change.

The theorem correctly takes the supremum of finite Bessel bounds and requires no completeness. The only frozen-context mismatch was the orthonormal-family interface, now repaired under its own targeted rejection; no change to this theorem is warranted.
The cited recursion theorem iterates a fixed self-map, whereas the update depended on the external stage n. The repair puts n into the state and iterates a fixed map on N x P(H).
The cofinality fact took the maximum of the empty finite set. The repair handles F empty with N=0 and applies the finite-maximum lemma only to nonempty F.
A7 incorrectly claimed the complex L2 pairing theorem assumed Countable Choice. The repair assigns choice only to the cited completeness theorems and records that the pairing theorem is choice-free.

The definition allowed an arbitrary Banach fibre even though its local trivializations were diffeomorphisms to U times F under the library's second-countable manifold convention. For a non-second-countable F that target is not a library Banach manifold. The repair requires F's norm topology to be second countable and types operator-valued transition maps chartwise.

The witnesses were proved to have a common complexification and to be nonisomorphic, but the refutation never established the statement's semisimplicity hypothesis. The repair computes nondegenerate real Killing matrices for both witnesses and applies Cartan's criterion.

The proof repeatedly invoked Tonelli while citing only the L1 Fubini theorem. The repair adds the exact sigma-finite Tonelli dependency and also states the measurable positive/negative-part decomposition correctly.
A4 called the second inner-product argument linear under the complex convention. The repair uses conjugate-linearity and its additive part for the span argument.
The sine zero-set theorem did not supply cos(m pi)=(-1)^m. The repair cites the pi-shift formula and derives the cosine values by integer induction, then refreshes the ledger.

The example invoked the semisimple root-space definition and theorem for sl2(C) without assuming or proving semisimplicity. The repair first computes the nondegenerate Killing matrix and applies Cartan's criterion, then identifies the Cartan subalgebra and root spaces.

The local slice condition permits nonisomorphic model spaces on different components, but the definition claimed that all of S is modelled on one local E0. The repair states the induced structure componentwise, proves local constancy of the model type, and defines T_pS through the component containing p.

Step 2.1 used a tail bound epsilon as though it were epsilon squared, and the completeness proof omitted the scalar-field completeness needed for coordinate limits. The repair applies tail control at epsilon squared and cites finite-dimensional Banach completeness for the scalar field.

The normalizer proof incorrectly inferred that each individual weight bracket lies in t from the fact that their sum lies in t. The repair uses uniqueness of the direct weight-space decomposition to make each nonzero-weight component vanish.

A5 attributed the full complementary-tail identity to finite Bessel and Pythagoras alone. The repair explicitly combines Parseval, the finite residual identity, and the nonnegative-family splitting identity.

A4 incorrectly inferred absolute continuity with respect to Lebesgue measure merely from a carrier of full measure; the repaired proof identifies the absolutely continuous carrier through the Lebesgue decomposition.

The proof incorrectly treated the adjoint Cayley transform as the Cayley transform of the same extension; the repair proves directly that the extension Cayley transform maps the two deficiency spaces onto one another.
The density argument used kernel-range orthogonality without an exact supplier; the repair declares and cites the local kernel-range orthogonality lemma.
The cutoff fact had the direction of convergence reversed, invalidating dominated convergence; the repair uses cutoffs increasing pointwise to one.
The proof invoked a domain-sensitive second resolvent identity despite allowing arbitrary self-adjoint domains; the repair uses the bounded resolvent identity furnished by the resolvent-star lemma.

The repair cites the exact basis theorem, verifies or source-grounds each displayed simple system, corrects the A_n indexing boundary, and closes an incomplete E8 reflection check.

L1 restated the irreducible connected-diagram tree theorem as if every finite-type Cartan matrix had a tree diagram. The repair restores the irreducibility/connectedness qualification; the cycle counterexample and positive-definiteness computation remain unchanged.

The proof inferred that |lambda|^n<=||V^n|| was impossible merely because ||V^n|| tends to zero, which fails for 0<|lambda|<1. The repair divides the explicit factorial norm bound by |lambda|^n and proves by a ratio calculation that the quotient tends to zero. It also proves non-self-adjointness directly by unequal pairings.

The remark claimed classification of all complex semisimple Lie algebras while citing only the simple-algebra classification. The repair distinguishes connected diagrams for simple algebras from finite disjoint unions for semisimple algebras and cites the exact corollary.

F1 restated nonmetacompactness as existence of a cover with no point-finite refinement, impossible under the bare containment definition because the empty family always refines. The repair uses the exact condition: no point-finite open refining cover of the space.

The so_{2n+1} block display was ill-typed and did not solve AJ+JA^T=0. The repair uses row u and column w in the correct transposed positions, fixes the independently reversed transpose order in the bracket computation, and states n>=1 where nonzero properness is claimed.

The repair defines the composite on the proved-open set J=gamma^{-1}[U], establishes [0,1] subset J, and applies the chain rule only on J.
